Component 1 regime, 23-Oct-26 (risk-off confirmed and broadening: the discount-rate squeeze now a positioning wash-out in the artificial intelligence complex with credit leading it, bonds rallied as a hedge for the first time this cycle while the Fed still hikes in December, the US 10-year near 5.10%, Brent $111, French sovereign stress spilling into Italy, European defensives leading cyclicals on all five windows and breadth in the bottom fifth of three years; sources present 2026-W43): two houses call a cyclical upturn, DNB Carnegie (22 Oct) reading Sandvik and Metso as a new mining cycle and Danske (18 Oct) heavy trucks and pulp and paper turning, and Goldman's economists (16 Oct) have US industrial production beating with machinery and electrical equipment near peak capacity use; against it, Danske's own warning that most cyclical exposure is 'more or less at all-time highs' with 'cost inflation emerging', a risk-off regime confirmed on all five defensive windows, and Relative strength per 31-relative-strength.md, 2026-10-23 against 2026-08-21, not week on week: D now, C prior at industry level. memo.verdict: Park. Neutral, leaning bearish at 4.218 EUR (2026-09-29); conviction medium. Ariston is a self-help recovery inside a European residential heating industry whose structure is getting worse; the shares already pay for the part of the recovery the company controls and price the part it does not at even odds, so the 'Modal return' is 4.7 percent a year over eighteen months and 8.1 percent a year over three years against the framework's 20 percent bar. The case clears the bar only below about 3.40 EUR on the eighteen-month test (about 3.10 EUR on the three-year test), where the shares stood between April and June 2026. The park rule is triggered twice (business quality E 2, BB 2 at D; management RA 3, E 1, BB 4 at D) and the record does not argue past it. What brings the case back: a price near 3.40 EUR on unchanged evidence, or the three monitoring tests passed at the current price (German BAFA applications above 25,000 a month through November 2026; German heat-pump pricing better than -5 percent year on year by 31-Oct-26; Q3 2026 adjusted EBIT margin at or above 5.7 percent on 4-Nov-26). Not an invalidation: the case is watched cheaply on monthly series for the price or the evidence that would make it a case.
case: The thesis. Ariston is a self-help recovery inside a European residential heating industry whose structure is getting worse. At 4.218 EUR the shares already pay for the part of the recovery the company controls and price the part it does not control at even odds; the modal return is about 5 percent a year over eighteen months against a 20 percent bar; the case clears the bar only below about 3.40 EUR.

The change is internal and real. Five dated, funded things at once: Fit-2-Win (50 EURm of permanent savings by 2027; about 20 EURm delivered by late 2025; after 80 EURm of opex and capex cuts and 468 net headcount cut in 2024; World Class Manufacturing at 32 sites); Riello (completed 1-Jul-26; enterprise value 289 EURm; about 5x EV/EBITDA including 25 EURm of run-rate synergies by 2030, 8.2x pre-synergy against Ariston's own 7.5x; about 370 EURm of cash out; a starting EBITDA margin about 9 percent against the group's 11.5 percent; 160 mono-brand agents; commercial and industrial combustion); the Niš cylinder-insourcing plant in Serbia (inaugurated 11-Dec-25; 30,000 square metres; 75 EURm); the Lennox water-heater joint venture in North America (50.1 percent Ariston; launched March 2026 through 300-plus stores and 10,000 dealers; ahead of its internal first-year targets; a 10 USDbn market where A. O. Smith, Rheem and Bradford White hold about 90 percent; meaningful revenue from 2027); a chief executive three years in, reappointed 5-May-26. Only one of twelve internal forces is strong on the screen's standard (cost discipline B); guidance was confirmed, not raised, after the Q2 beat; the screen's rule (three strong forces, or chief-executive change plus a guidance increase) is not met, so internal forces rate C. Red-flag check: no caretaker chief executive; a "PowerPoint transformation" partly (Destination 2030 targets a 10 percent margin reached twice since 2010); no trivial guidance rise; no crown-jewel sale; empire-building plausible ("We want to be the consolidator"); leverage not dangerous; no debt-funded buyback.

The external forces run the other way and are larger. Six of seven categories are headwinds. Competition F: Chinese heat-pump exports to Europe +45 percent in Q1 2026 (Midea, from about 5 percent European share in 2024 toward 15 percent); Chinese units 20 to 50 percent cheaper; Italian air-to-water heat-pump pricing about -10 percent in Q1 2026 and about -12 percent in Q2 2026; German unit pricing -14 percent year on year in Q4 2025; Carrier's European volumes +20 percent in Q2 2026 with its Climate Solutions margin -70 basis points to 7.2 percent on promotions; counter-evidence, Nibe reports stable core pricing and installers rarely switch once trained. Political and regulatory D: Germany's Building Modernization Act (10-Jul-26) removed the 65 percent renewable-heating mandate; the BEG cost cap cut from 30,000 EUR to 28,000 EUR from 21-Jul-26, saving 2.1 EURbn through an income-targeted model; Italy's Superbonus 110 to 70 percent in 2024 and 65 percent from 1-Jan-25; France's MaPrimeRénov' reopened 23-Feb-26 with 3.6 EURbn but narrower; the US 2,000 USD credit rescinded 31-Dec-25; BEG funding legally intact to 2029 at up to 70 to 80 percent reimbursement. Supply side D: copper +38 percent, aluminium +34 percent, polypropylene +29 percent, steel +11 percent year to date at 30-Jun-26; transport +10.8 EURm in H1 2026; service costs +20.3 EURm to 260.3 EURm; hedges about 80 percent of steel, rolling up to two years; raw materials 46.5 percent of FY2024 revenue; Section 232 exposure at Saltillo. Demand D: German approvals 27,000 a month in Q1 2026 (+28 percent), read by the sell-side as a pull-forward ahead of the 21-Jul-26 step-down; monthly applications 37,500 in December 2025 to 14,200 in January 2026; German completions -18 percent in 2025 to 206,600, permits +15.4 percent in the five months to May 2026 (104,700); French starts +32 percent year to date; German household payback lengthening from 26 years to 37 by 2028 and 46 by 2030; the US 2029 Department of Energy rule a real structural force but small for Ariston before 2029. Disruption D: utilities installing with in-house teams; subscription models (Reliance's 30 percent Ontario water-heater share); R32 clearance discounting ahead of the 1-Jan-27 F-gas ban, against Ariston's R290 capability (Elco AEROTOP Red Dot 2026; the Mainburg R290 line). Macro D: ECB deposit rate to 2.25 percent in June 2026; German ten-year mortgage rates about 4 percent; consumer confidence -19 in April 2026; Europe 72 percent of revenue with translation unhedged (a 2 percent move is 1.5 EURm of pre-tax profit). The company's own cycle C: troughed FY2024, turning (FY2025 organic +3.0 percent, 7.1 percent margin; Q2 2026 +5.2 percent, 5.7 percent). Catch-all D: the Q4 2026 industry-wide R32 clearance will distort the Q4 comparison. The supports: the electricity-to-gas ratio improved to 2.4x to 2.5x from above 3x, and the first-half German approvals. The 'Demand Inflection' test is not met: capacity utilisation 40 to 60 percent in 2026; demand growth about 10 percent against 42 percent capacity growth.
counter_case: At Building Block 1, the strongest version. The H1 2026 beat shows the operating leverage is real: Q2 2026 EBIT rose 28.3 percent on revenue up 7.4 percent. Consensus FY2027 EPS of 0.410 EUR (+20 percent on FY2026) is not heroic: it is Riello's full year at about 5x EV/EBITDA post-synergy, Fit-2-Win's completion and 3 to 4 percent organic growth. Riello is accretive by high teens including run-rate synergies. The Lennox joint venture beat its internal first-year targets in a 10 USDbn market with a 2029 regulatory catalyst. The energy-price ratio has improved to 2.4x to 2.5x; German permits are up 15.4 percent; the most bearish house has moved to Hold; six of eight brokers are at Buy with a 4.56 EUR target. The shares fell from 5.5599 to 3.084 EUR and still trade at 9.35x, below their ten-year median, on earnings just shown to have operating leverage. If the German recovery is real and pricing holds, the stock earns the median multiple on a 0.49 EUR FY2028 and returns 20 percent a year from here. The recovery is under-modelled and the thesis is material.

What the record concedes: the operating leverage is real; H1 2026 was better than the sell-side modelled; our own FY2027 figure (0.39 EUR) could prove too low if the Q3 margin holds; Riello's price is fair once synergies arrive and its mono-brand channel is a genuine defensive asset; the balance sheet is sound; the drivers are few and trackable; the value at the spring low was there.
triggers: - The open question the recommendation names: whether the German recovery is a pull-forward; it resolves within two quarters.
- Re-entry on price: near 3.40 EUR on unchanged evidence (the eighteen-month test); about 3.10 EUR on the three-year test.

- Re-entry on evidence at the current price, all three: German BAFA applications above 25,000 a month through November 2026; German heat-pump pricing better than -5 percent year on year by 31-Oct-26 (Morgan Stanley's quarterly check); Q3 2026 adjusted EBIT margin at or above 5.7 percent on 4-Nov-26. Applications holding and Q3 European organic growth above 3 percent would move demand from even odds to probable; a Q3 margin at or above 5.7 percent would raise our FY2027 EPS toward the consensus median.

- Alarm levels: BAFA applications below 15,000 a month, or a sequential fall of more than 15 percent by November 2026; Italian or German heat-pump pricing worse than -5 percent year on year by 31-Oct-26; Q3 2026 adjusted EBIT margin below 5.7 percent; copper spot more than 10 percent above the H1 2026 level.

- Invalidate levels: German organic heat-pump revenue down more than 15 percent quarter on quarter by Q4 2026 with stable approvals; heat-pump pricing erosion above 20 percent year on year in any quarter to 2027; Riello cumulative synergies below 15 EURm by end-2027; industry capacity utilisation below 50 percent through Q1 2027; German permits down for three consecutive quarters to Q1 2027.

- Confirmations on the second-tier drivers: the Lennox joint venture at 75 to 100 USDm annualised by Q4 2026; Riello cumulative synergies 12 to 15 EURm by end-2027; net debt to EBITDA back toward 2x by the FY2026 year-end.
